sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Settings template
sections.what: Lists each setting with a short comment. Required settings come first, then optional groups.
sections.why: Documents what the app needs so setup is not guesswork.
sections.watch_out: Do not place real secrets in this file, because it is committed to the repository.

summary: A template that lists every setting the app reads, with blank or placeholder values and short explanations. It is copied to .env to start.
purpose: Shows a developer which settings exist and which are required.
why: The header says to copy it to .env, and that values in the shell override the file.
how: Groups the settings into required ones (database address, signing key, login accounts), an optional skip-login switch for development, ports, AI features, web search, object storage, and tuning. Every optional setting is commented out, so it stays off until someone sets it.
inputs: None. It is copied by a person or by a script.
outputs: None directly. It serves as a reference.
risks: Placeholder values must be replaced. The skip-login switches are dangerous if left on in a shared environment, although the comment says they are ignored in production. Real secrets must not be placed in this committed file.
debug: If the app says a feature is not configured, check the setting is uncommented and has a value. If login fails, regenerate the login entry with the setup script.
